_comment: ADR citation closure gate (DATA, not code). A mechanical de-stale pass rewrote ADR path citations onto the ten live apex ADRs under docs/decisions/. Every rewritten path is a VALID PATH TO AN EXISTING FILE, so a link checker passes all of them; many nonetheless point at an apex that never claimed the ADR the surrounding sentence is about. Only checking MEANING against an independent supersession oracle catches that. The oracle is built from BOTH frontmatter sides — apex `supersedes:` and member `superseded_by:` — because supersession CHAINS through archived intermediates (ADR-0110 -> ADR-0363 -> ADR-0701; ADR-0349 -> ADR-0515 -> ADR-0700) and because members exist that declare a successor no apex acknowledges. ONLY those frontmatter keys are parsed: bodies mention ADR ids constantly, one archived ADR even carries a fenced `superseded_by:` block naming itself, and grepping whole files produces false matches. ALL repo-specifics are DATA — another repo adopts this gate by repointing these values.

measured._comment: ENFORCED shrink-only ceilings, pinned by EQUALITY in live_tree_findings_equal_the_frozen_ceilings. Originally recorded as inert measurements with the gate deliberately red; that could not land, because affected-set test-health counts any failing test as a regression against a baseline of zero, so a permanently-red gate is correct and unmergeable. Equality rather than <= is deliberate and matches ci/facade/corpus-index-coverage: a NEW finding exceeds the ceiling and fails, and a REPAIRED finding falls below it and also fails, forcing the ceiling down in the same change. The census values are the anti-vacuity anchor — a repaired corpus and a collapsed walk both report fewer findings, and only the census distinguishes them.

measured._review_remeasure_2026_08_08: Detection was widened by review repair, so these ceilings were re-frozen in the same change. rejected_authority 2 -> 3: the rule read only `context`, but scan_line moves an id out of `context` when the line ALSO writes it as a decisions/ path, so `[ADR-0347](decisions/ADR-0347-...)` on docs/AGENTS.md — the surface that MANDATES it as active doctrine while its frontmatter says Rejected — was invisible. It now reads both halves. adr_citation_dangling_path 1979 is a NEW code: a decisions/ path naming a non-apex used to be a silent `continue`, and docs/decisions/ holds only ADR-0700..0709, so every citation of an archived id by that path is a broken link. Composition, measured at FILE level rather than finding level: 51 .md files carry such citations against 6 .rs, 7 .json and a handful of others, so it is overwhelmingly real broken links in doctrine surfaces rather than test fixtures. An earlier draft gave a finding-level '161 vs 9' that review flagged as unreproduced; the file-level figures above are re-derivable with `git grep -l 'docs/decisions/ADR-0[0-6][0-9][0-9]'`; no blanket .rs exemption was added, because that would also blind the gate to genuine references in doc comments. archived_with_successor 423 -> 425 because the floor now counts BOTH oracle sides, which is what it claims to guard. files_scanned 16496 -> 16512: the census moved onto `git ls-files` (the boundary every other gate uses) and stopped skipping the 15 tracked symlinks that entry.file_type() never reported as files. citation_lines is unchanged at 8899, which is the cross-check that the boundary move did not widen the corpus. mismatch/asymmetry/unresolvable/ambiguous are all unchanged.
measured._dangling_vs_mismatch: The two citation codes are disjoint by construction. adr_citation_dangling_path fires when the cited id is not a live apex — the path does not resolve, so there is nothing to compare meaning against. adr_citation_closure_mismatch fires only when the cited id IS a live apex and every resolvable ADR named on the line closes onto a different one. A bare id that is itself a live apex is no longer counted as evidence, because resolve() returns Live(itself) for it and that made every apex-to-apex cross reference an unsuppressable false accusation.
measured._rebase_remeasure_2026_08_08: Re-frozen against dev at 8097ce74c, which now carries PR #1617's 85 citation repairs. mismatch 340 -> 255 is exactly those 85, and the equality ratchet REFUSED the build until the ceiling followed — the ratchet working as designed on its first real occasion. rejected_authority 2 -> 3 is the review fix landing: the gate now sees docs/AGENTS.md:57, a Rejected ADR cited only inside a link path, which the old rule could not reach because scan_line moved the id out of `context` when the line also wrote it as a decisions/ path. That instance was findings 1+2 of the review and is the reason this gate needed fixing at all.

measured._corpus_pin_2026_08_08: The corpus census (files_scanned, citation_lines, adr_records) is now PINNED BY EQUALITY in live_tree_findings_equal_the_frozen_ceilings, and is asserted BEFORE any finding count. A high-effort review proved the gate could be turned green without repairing one citation: append two entries to exempt_path_prefixes, lower the two ceilings in the same file, and all ten tests passed while 281 findings silently left the enforced set. The corpus definition and the ceilings share this file, so a policy-only edit satisfied a ratchet meant to require repair, and the census values this block already called 'the anti-vacuity anchor' were asserted by NO test. Pinning them closes it: the same exploit now fails with 'files_scanned: observed 16170, frozen 16519' before a finding count is compared. Repair moves finding counts and leaves the corpus alone; narrowing moves the corpus. The ratchet can now tell them apart. files_scanned 16512->16519 and citation_lines 8895->8896 are the seven completion packets PR #1618 merged, re-frozen here in the same change the pin was added.

The two effects are independent and neither cancels the other, which matters because a coincidental zero is exactly the case the deletions entry above warns about: this zero is the sum of a measured +1/-1 and a measured 0, not an unexplained no-op. The OWNERS file is deliberately NOT reachability-registered: ci/facade/artifact-accountability/tests/total_accounting.rs::owners_files_are_never_registered_in_the_reachability_registry forbids it, because OWNERS files are accounted by construction (justification_ref `owners-schema`).

measured._review_fixes_2026_08_08: mismatch 255 -> 252: three FALSE POSITIVES removed, not three citations repaired. An `adr-archive/ADR-NNNN-...` link is the sentence stating that ADR is historical, but scan_line routed it to `context`, which evaluate reads as residual evidence of the sentence's subject. A correct line naming a historical ADR beside a live apex therefore fired a mismatch. Fixing it LOWERS the count, which is why the equality ratchet demanded a re-freeze in the same change. Also fixed here, latent rather than live: parse_supersession matched block-list items only at the exact prefix '  - ', so a supersedes/superseded_by written at four-space indent was silently dropped in a parser contracted to fail closed. No ADR uses that form today, so the counts are unchanged; three regression tests cover both fixes and the nested-key case that must stay ignored.

product_contract.born_blocking: Born BLOCKING and RED. Unlike a coverage ratchet there is no defensible ceiling here: a citation that resolves to the wrong apex is not debt to be burned down, it is a statement that is false today, and freezing a ceiling would licence the corpus to keep lying at its current rate. The gate reports every mismatch and fails until they are repaired.
product_contract.both_sides_oracle: Successor edges are the UNION of member `superseded_by` and apex `supersedes` membership, walked transitively to a live apex. An apex-side-only map misses chained members; a member-side-only map misses the members no apex acknowledges. Either alone manufactures false accusations.
product_contract.false_positive_guard: A citation line often names several ADRs — a range endpoint, a lineage, a see-also. A line is a defect only when at least one named ADR resolves AND NONE resolves to the cited apex. A line citing two apexes, or naming an ADR whose closure is ambiguous, is skipped rather than guessed.
product_contract.rejected_authority_scope: The Rejected-ADR rule is scoped to `authority_surfaces` — the files that ARE the governance contract. Repo-wide it would fire on thousands of historical mentions, filename ranges and provenance notes, none of which claim authority. Scoped, it catches the real instances: root CLAUDE.md citing ADR-0111 (Rejected) as merge-queue authority.
product_contract.anti_vacuity: Five floors. The first four guard the CENSUS (ADR records, live apexes, citation lines, authority surfaces). The third — min_archived_with_successor — guards the ORACLE, and is not redundant with the others: frontmatter parsing can silently return no edges while every ADR file and every citation is still found, leaving both censuses intact and the oracle empty. An empty oracle resolves nothing, so no citation can ever be called wrong, and the gate reports a flawless corpus. Only a floor on the edge count catches that.
product_contract.known_limitations: Detection requires RESIDUAL evidence: a citation whose line no longer names any ADR carries nothing to check it against, and the de-stale pass rewrote the filename slug too. The measurable defect class is therefore a lower bound on the real one. Only supersession is modelled — `amends`/`amended_by` carry authority changes this gate does not evaluate. Attribution is LINE-SCOPED by deliberate refusal: the subject of a citation is read only from the line carrying it, so a subject stated on an adjacent line or in an enclosing heading is invisible and that citation is simply never judged. Widening attribution to the surrounding block was refused rather than deferred — a heuristic that guesses which nearby sentence owns a link manufactures accusations against correct citations, and this gate's whole value is that a finding is a statement that is false today. The consequence is under-detection, which is the safe direction and is already accounted for by the lower-bound clause above. The cases where attribution WOULD be ambiguous are skipped rather than guessed: a line citing two or more apex paths produces no mismatch finding at all, and a bare id that is itself a live apex is not counted as evidence, so the any-match rule is order-independent over the resolvable ids and never depends on which link came first.

purpose: Make a syntactically valid, semantically wrong ADR citation impossible to reintroduce, by resolving every cited apex against an independent both-sides supersession closure instead of checking that the path exists.
